TutorialPageProperties.Description:
The number under each unit shows how many units of that type are ready for use.

The "+" icon indicates that the unit of that type can be trained. Not every unit is available for training. Some units are unlocked by decrees or story decisions.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Available Units

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
The units that are currently out on the battlefield are shown in the "DEPLOYED" panel below.

The number under each unit shows how many units are deployed at the moment.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Deployed Units

TutorialPageProperties.Description: To increase your resources to train units, sign decrees to build factories, make trade deals or make decisions in favour of the military.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Gaining More Resources

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
The "IN TRAINING" section shows the units currently in training. They will be available to deploy in the next turn.

You can remove units from training by clicking on them in the "IN TRAINING" panel and cancel training.

Once you hit the "Train" button below, the units in training are locked in and can't be removed anymore. Plan carefully before committing to training units as resources might be limited.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: "In Training"

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
Resources like equipment, tanks, trucks etc. are shown here. Spend these to train units.

Hover over any unit type in "Available" below to see its training costs.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Resources

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
Any unit that is not within the protective range of a friendly Anti-Air tile <sprite name="antiair"> can be the target of an air strike.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Air strikes will cause damage to a unit's <sprite name="organization">. Struck supporting units will be removed from the current battle they are supporting.

Any player unit that is not within the range of an enemy Anti-Air tile <sprite name="antiair"> and is in an active battle, can be supported from the air. This will give the unit a bonus on its <sprite name="attack"> or <sprite name="defence">.

Both air strikes and air support have a cooldown of several turns before being available for use again.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Air Strikes and Air Support

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
\u2022 A Land Unit can attack adjacent enemy units or cities with > 0 <sprite name="organization"> if they are not part of a battle yet. Supporting units, that are part of a battle, can also be attacked.
\u2022 A Naval Unit can attack, even if its several tiles away. The unit will automatically move to an adjacent tile and attack.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Attack

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
By selecting a unit and clicking on it's own tile again, it can be Fortified <sprite name="fortify">. This will give a bonus of +1 <sprite name="defence"> and heal +1 <sprite name="organization"> per turn. 
<indent=5%> \u2022 A fortified unit can not move or support until the next turn.
<indent=5%> \u2022 A fortified unit with 0 <sprite name="organization"> can still be overrun <sprite name="overrun">.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Fortify

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
Attacking or being attacked will trigger a battle.
<indent=5%> \u2022 A battle that has equal points on both sides will end in favor of the defender. The attacker will lose 1 <sprite name="organization">.
<indent=5%> \u2022 If a defending unit drops to 0 <sprite name="organization"> it either gets overrun by the attacker or pushed back to a free adjacent tile if available.
<indent=5%> \u2022 If a defending city drops to 0 <sprite name="organization"> it will change its allegiance.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Attacking an enemy unit that has 0 <sprite name="organization">, results in overrunning <sprite name="overrun"> them and overtaking their tile.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Land Battle

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
Mountains <sprite name="mountain">:
<indent=5%> \u2022 Mountaineers can move freely from, to and on <sprite name="mountain"> while also getting a bonus on stats. Regular units get a <sprite name="defence"> bonus but a <sprite name="attack"> penalty while also being locked <sprite name="movementlocked"> from further actions for the remaining turn after moving to <sprite name="mountain">.</indent>
Fortifications <sprite name="fortlevel1"><sprite name="fortlevel2">:
<indent=5%> \u2022 These tiles give the occupying units a bonus on <sprite name="defence">. </indent>
Anti-Air <sprite name="antiair">:
<indent=5%> \u2022 These tiles protect occupying and adjacent friendly units from being bombed <sprite name="bombed"> in an Air Strike. Protection only applies to units of the same allegiance as the tile.</indent>
Coastal Artillery <sprite name="coastalartillery">:
<indent=5%> \u2022 These tiles will deal damage to enemy Naval Units on adjacent tiles. The tile allegiance determines the effect on the adjacent unit.</indent>
Air Field <sprite name="airbase">:
<indent=5%> \u2022 These tiles hold the Air Strike power of the enemy. Capturing them will lower the enemies Air Strike capabilities. </indent>
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Map Overview

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
\u2022 Default: Move to any free adjacent tile, or swap positions with a friendly unit.
\u2022 Supply Lines: Vehicles can move up to 2 tiles on Supply Lines.
\u2022 Mountains <sprite name="mountain"> : Units other than Mountaineers get movement locked <sprite name="movementlocked">.
\u2022 Sea: Naval Units have a larger range and can move to any free tile on the sea that is not blockaded <sprite name="blockaded">.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Movement

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
<indent=5%> \u2022 Naval Units can attack other Naval Units even when they are further away. The unit will automatically move to the enemy unit when attacking.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Naval Units can not attack Land Units directly.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Unlike Land Units, Naval Units can move away and disengage from a battle. This will cost 1 Action Point.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Naval Battle

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
<indent=5%> \u2022 Naval Units can support each other in battle.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Naval Units can also support Land Units adjacent to Sea Tiles, unlike Land Units who can not support Naval Battles. 
<indent=5%> \u2022 Naval Units have two different <sprite name="support">, one for Land Battle Support and one for Naval Battle Support.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Naval Support

TutorialPageProperties.Description: \u2022 Capture all objectives <sprite name="objective"> and hold them. Gain as much territory as possible and thwart enemy attacks to protect it.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Objective

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
Depending on the kind of military investments, Paratroopers or Marines can be deployed behind enemy lines.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Paratroopers can be deployed on highlighted tiles.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Marines can be deployed on highlighted shore tiles..
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Paratroopers and Marines

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
Supply Lines are roadways that supply cities and units and give them advantages.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Cities that are supplied have higher <sprite name="defence"> and units on active Supply Lines will automatically give +1 <sprite name="organization"> at the end of a turn. 
<indent=5%> \u2022 Enemy Supply Lines are orange, player Supply Lines are blue and cut off Supply Lines are grey.
<indent=5%> \u2022 Enemy Reinforcements may spawn on active enemy Supply Lines.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Supply Lines

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
\u2022 Units can support friendly units in battle. Their <sprite name="support"> will be added to the battle calculation.
\u2022 Friendly units have to be adjacent to the attacking unit or adjacent to the defending unit to be able to support the battle. 
\u2022 Ships can support land and naval battles but Land Units can not support naval Battles.
\u2022 Enemy Land Units will automatically support battles when attacking or being attacked.
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Support

TutorialPageProperties.Description:
Units have 4 different stats: 
<indent=5%> \u2022 Organization <sprite name="organization">
<indent=5%> \u2022 Attack <sprite name="attack">
<indent=5%> \u2022 Defense <sprite name="defence">
<indent=5%> \u2022 Support <sprite name="support">
TutorialPageProperties.Title: Units
